conventions.convention: Def(A) is the Replacement-collected set of subsets {x in A : (A, in) satisfies phi(x,a1,...,an)} for coded formulas and finite parameter tuples (unused variables allowed, parameters need not be distinct); Def(empty) is the separate clause {empty} because the empty carrier is not treated as a structure.

Satisfaction in a nonempty structure is compared only on finite tuples (extended to assignments by a fixed element), and internal/external agreement does not assert equality of the assignment spaces (A^omega)^N = A^omega.

L is generated by L_0 = empty, L_{alpha+1} = Def(L_alpha), L_lambda = union of earlier levels at nonzero limits; x in L abbreviates existence of a level containing x (a definable class, not a set union); constructible rank rho_L(x) is the unique alpha with x a member of L_{alpha+1} minus L_alpha.

The canonical order keeps the old order, puts every old element before every new element of L_{alpha+1} minus L_alpha, and orders new elements by their least definition codes under a once-and-for-all natural-number formula/arity coding; the same construction performed inside L gives the identical relation.

OD is unique definability in some V_theta with theta > 0 and finitely many ordinal parameters below theta (set satisfaction, not a universe truth predicate); HOD = {x : TC({x}) is contained in OD} with the root-inclusive TC convention.

Forcing order: q <= p means q is stronger; filters are nonempty, upward closed and internally downward directed; density is forall p exists q in D (q <= p); M-genericity meets every dense D that belongs to M, with M's countability external; no largest condition, countability or generic existence is assumed.

P-names are sets of pairs with the name first and the condition second, generated by N_{alpha+1} = P(N_alpha x P); name rank is the supremum of predecessor ranks plus one and is explicitly distinct from the membership rank of a condition.

val_G(tau) = {val_G(sigma) : some p in G has (sigma,p) in tau} and M[G] = {val_G(tau) : tau a P-name in M}; the notation asserts neither genericity of G nor that M[G] satisfies ZF, and G may be empty (all valuations then empty).

Check names use every condition as coefficient (check x = {(check y,p) : y in x, p in P}) and dot G = {(check p,p) : p in P}; no largest (weakest) condition is required, and the top-only recursion is only a remark.

Boolean semantics uses coefficients in all of B including 0, the E/I recursion with empty join 0 and empty meet 1, and existential values as joins of the set of attained matrix values; only formula-by-formula definability is asserted, with no uniform truth predicate and no external completeness inference.

Inaccessible means uncountable, regular and strong limit (2^mu < kappa for every cardinal mu < kappa); weakly inaccessible (mere limit) is kept separate; Mahlo means the uncountable regular cardinals below kappa are stationary; no existence is asserted.

Kappa-completeness is closure under intersections indexed by ordinals below kappa, with the empty intersection equal to I; measurable = uncountable kappa carrying a nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilter on the full power set of kappa; normality = every regressive function on a measure-one set omitting 0 is constant on a measure-one subset.

Universe ultrapowers use Scott representatives [f]_U = the U-equivalent functions of least membership rank, with E given by U-large coordinate membership; elementary embeddings are definable class functions with elementarity verified formula by formula and set-restrictions being sets, and no Global Choice is assumed.

Weak compactness is inaccessibility plus the tree property (every kappa-tree has a cofinal branch), and kappa -> (kappa)^2_mu is the homogeneous-set arrow with the color cardinal fixed nonzero; the tree/partition equivalence is not assumed in the definition.

L_{kappa,kappa} formulas are well-founded set syntax trees with conjunctions/disjunctions and quantifier blocks of length below kappa; satisfaction is defined only for set structures by recursion on the tree; the empty conjunction is true and the empty disjunction false; compactness statements are properties, not theorems.

Fine measures live on P_kappa(lambda) = {x subset of lambda : |x| < kappa} and contain every point cone; strong compactness is extension of every kappa-complete filter on every set; lambda-supercompactness is a normal fine kappa-complete ultrafilter on P_kappa(lambda).

A Laver anticipation function ell : kappa -> V_kappa must anticipate every set x at every cardinal lambda >= kappa by a supercompactness embedding with crit kappa, j(kappa) > lambda, lambda-closure and j(ell)(kappa) = x; only ell's values below kappa need lie in V_kappa.

An externally supplied M-generic Boolean filter G contained in B minus {0} is a proper ultrafilter and selects ground joins and meets: the M-join of A lies in G iff A meets G, and the M-meet of A lies in G iff A is contained in G, for ground families A in M only.

Solovay densities: nu_a(c) is the unique value taken U-large by i maps to m(c meet a_i), and h_a is the almost-everywhere class of [0,1]-valued measurable functions with integral over c equal to nu_a(c); all identities are representative-independent and live in the original probability space, not in a generic extension.

load_bearing.statement: An inaccessible cardinal is an uncountable regular strong limit cardinal: 2^mu < kappa for every cardinal mu < kappa. ... An inaccessible kappa is Mahlo if {alpha < kappa : alpha is an uncountable regular cardinal} is stationary.

the following are equivalent: kappa is measurable; kappa carries a normal measure; kappa is the critical point of a definable elementary embedding j : V -> M into a transitive class, under the set-restriction convention.

L_0 = empty, L_{alpha+1} = Def(L_alpha), L_lambda = union of earlier levels (lambda a nonzero limit) ... Write x in L for exists alpha (x in L_alpha) ... Define the constructible rank rho_L(x) = alpha.
j(alpha) = alpha for every alpha < kappa, and kappa <= pi([id_kappa]_U) < j(kappa). In particular the critical point, the least ordinal moved by j, is kappa.

|V_alpha| < kappa for every alpha < kappa, every x in V_kappa has size less than kappa, and every set of fewer than kappa elements of V_kappa belongs to V_kappa. ... The strong-limit cardinals below kappa contain a club subset of kappa.
val_G(tau) = {val_G(sigma) : exists p in G with (sigma,p) in tau} ... M[G] = {val_G(tau) : tau in M is a P-name}. The notation asserts neither genericity of G nor that M[G] is a model of ZF.

a proper filter U on I is kappa-complete if the intersection of any eta < kappa of its members lies in U. The intersection with no factors is I ... A measurable cardinal is an uncountable kappa carrying a nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilter on the full power set of kappa.
a filter G contained in P is M-generic if G meets D for every dense D contained in P with D in M. ... No largest condition, countability or existence of a generic filter is assumed by the definition.

[f]_U = {g : g U-equivalent to f, rank(g) = rho(f)} ... [f]_U E [g]_U iff {i : f(i) in g(i)} in U. ... A supplied definable elementary embedding j : V -> M means a definable class function into a definable transitive class M ... satisfying elementarity separately for each fixed first-order formula.

In ZF there is a parameter-free definable setlike class well-order of L. Each L_alpha is an initial segment, and its restriction is a set well-order. The canonical construction performed internally in L gives the same relation.

A Laver anticipation function is a set function ell : kappa -> V_kappa such that for every set x and every cardinal lambda >= kappa there is a supercompactness embedding j : V -> M with crit(j) = kappa, j(kappa) > lambda, lambda-sequences of M contained in M, and j(ell)(kappa) = x.

lambda-supercompactness is equivalent to the existence of a definable elementary embedding j : V -> M into a transitive class with critical point kappa, j(kappa) > lambda, and every ambient function from lambda to M belonging to M.
For every A in M with A contained in B, the M-join of A is in G iff A meets G, and the M-meet of A is in G iff A is contained in G.

For every coded membership formula phi and finite tuple a from A assigning all its free variables, satisfaction of phi[a] in (A, in) computed in N agrees with external satisfaction. This does not assert that (A^omega)^N = A^omega.
I(s,t) = the join over (u,b) in t of b meet E(s,u); E(s,t) = the meet of neg b or I(u,t) over both names ... the existential value is the join of {b : some B-name s has b = ||phi(s,t)||}.

the following are equivalent: kappa is strongly compact; every P_kappa(lambda) carries a fine kappa-complete ultrafilter; every less-than-kappa satisfiable set-sized L_{kappa,kappa} theory has a model; and the same compactness assertion holds for L_{kappa,omega}.
let s = pi([x maps to x]_U). Then j of lambda is contained in s, s is contained in j(lambda), and M satisfies |s| < j(kappa). U is normal if and only if s = j of lambda.
In ZF, for every nonempty G contained in P, val_G(check x) = x and val_G(dot G) = G. Hence for a transitive ZF model M containing P, M is contained in M[G] and G is in M[G].

the Scott ultrapower of V is well-founded if and only if U is countably complete. In that case its membership relation collapses to a transitive definable class M containing all ordinals, and the collapsed constant map is elementary, formula by formula.
For every a in B^I there is a unique almost-everywhere class of measurable h_a : X -> [0,1] such that for every c in B the integral of h_a over c is nu_a(c) and {i : m(c meet a_i) = nu_a(c)} is in U.

concerns.concern: Deep-theorem reconstruction compressed at its load-bearing point: step 4.1 asserts that M 'computes exactly the same least failure theta' (including every normal fine measure and its ultrapower evaluation) and step 5.1 that 'the transformed recursion at stage kappa ... selects a failing object a in H_{theta+}'. The reader must supply the verification that the definable least-failure predicate is absolute between V and M and that j(ell)(kappa)=a follows from the rule's clause in M; the original Laver source was not recovered and only Hamkins's sketch is cited. I found no false step, but correctness rests on this reconstruction.

Laver preparation, source not recovered. Compressed steps a reader must complete: 12.1 derives kappa-cc from a normal measure but leaves the common-extension step implicit (two-step decomposition at the inaccessible alpha plus the tail's <alpha-directed closure); 11.1/14.1 ('small prefix preserves regulars above its size') is sketched; 33.1 asserts that the stage-kappa activity test agrees in M via 'downward absoluteness explicitly' without detailing name-and-order absoluteness; 42.1 re-forms the descended measure as a W-set from the ground name set T and the <=chi-closed temporary forcing.

The Con(ZFC+strongly compact) implies Con(ZFC+PMEA) transfer rests on steps 2.1-3.1: the claim that the entire PMEA construction over a countable transitive ground uses only finitely many ZFC instances, so one finite Gamma suffices. No Gamma is exhibited and the two long suppliers (random-algebra cardinal preservation; Solovay/random-coordinate pullback) are not analysed instance by instance; a reader must verify the finite-fragment extraction, in particular that reflecting Gamma plus SC(kappa) (4.1) covers every axiom instance those suppliers use.

Step 5.1 justifies the value 1 of the logically true sentence exists x (x = f(c)) 'by step 4.1', but step 4.1 concerns T and H; the actual reason is that every node is the actual truth restriction of a structure, so every logically valid sentence gets value 1. The same implicit appeal to regularity (placing all sentences of a <kappa-sized family into one F_alpha) recurs in 4.1's equality-substitution and Boolean-clause claims.

Step 3.1 says the six basic axioms, internal Power Set, and 'Separation and Replacement in F4' establish ZF in L, but F4 names only thm-replacement-in-the-constructible-universe; internal Separation is available only through the dependency closure (F3 and F4 both depend on thm-separation-in-the-constructible-universe). The claim is true; the fact list is incomplete.
Step 1.1: 'The Boolean meet bounds r above and is nonzero, so a meet b is in G.' The meet is an upper bound of r (r <= a meet b), not a bound 'above' it; wording only, the inference is correct.

Step 4.1 proves mu^nu < kappa through the infinite-cardinal product estimate and then says 'This also covers finite cardinals', listing explicitly only mu^0=1, 0^nu=0 and 1^nu=1. For finite mu,nu >= 2 the bound is immediate (a finite cardinal is below kappa) but is not stated.
